title: Normalization of a derived direct-image composition unit
statement:
theorem normalizedDirectImageCompUnit {A B C : Scheme.{u}} (s : A ⟶ B) (t : B ⟶ C)
    (K : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings A.toRingedSpace)) (.up ℤ)) :
    (RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage (s ≫ t).toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app K ≫
      (schemeNormalizedDirectImageCompIso s t).inv.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj K) =
    (Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompUnit (Scheme.Modules.pushforward s)
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward t)).app K := by sorry

proof.text: Set f=s.toLRSHom.toShHom and g=t.toLRSHom.toShHom. Use the full recorded statement of lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_derivedModuleDirectImageComposition), not the bare Nonempty scheme composition theorem. It asserts existence of e: Rf_* followed by Rg_* is isomorphic to R(g o f)_*, together with, for every homotopy-category object K, eta_(g o f)(K);e.inv(Qh K)=eta_g(f_*^h K);Rg_*(eta_f(K)). By definition schemeNormalizedDirectImageCompIso s t is Classical.choose of precisely this existential for f and g. Classical.choose_spec evaluated at K therefore gives that equation for the selected comparison. The underlying ringed-space morphism of s followed by t is f followed by g, and schemeDerivedDirectImage is the corresponding ringed-space derived direct image. No properness, flatness, boundedness, or quasi-coherence hypothesis is used.

Write F=Scheme.Modules.pushforward s and G=Scheme.Modules.pushforward t. These are moduleDirectImage f and moduleDirectImage g by their definitions. Expand Functor.rightDerivedFunctorCompUnit F G: its component is the inverse mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso(Iso.refl(F followed by G)) mapped by Qh, followed by the second unit at F_*^h K and RG of the first unit at K; the associator components are identities. To check the initial comparison is the identity for arbitrary K, write K as the image of a complex I under the homotopy quotient (the quotient keeps objects). The comparison component is the quotient image of the identity chain map on G(F(I)), hence is the identity by functoriality; Qh also maps it to the identity. Removing identity factors gives exactly the right side of the equation in step 1, so that equation is the displayed conclusion.
